speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. I see you have double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand how long these symptoms have been present, could you tell me when they first started?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of fluctuation and improvement with rest is very telling. Do you notice your eyelids drooping significantly during the day, or have you experienced any difficulty swallowing or breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest, along with diplopia (double vision) and no sensory deficits or balance issues, is highly characteristic of this autoimmune neuromuscular disorder. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies AND REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Chest (to rule out thymoma).
